proposals.before: Qingong died; his grandson Yanzu succeeded.
proposals.after: Qingong died; his son Yanzu succeeded.
proposals.reason: Chinese 子彥祖 means his son Yanzu, not grandson; the idiomatic already has son correctly.

proposals.before: He served as Inspector-and-Protector on the staff of Liu Lao, Northern Pacification Army Adjutant.
proposals.after: He served as Inspector-and-Protector under Liu Laozhi, General Who Pacifies the North.
proposals.reason: Chinese 劉牢之鎮北參軍督護 identifies Liu Laozhi (牢之), not "Liu Lao", and 鎮北 is Laozhi's title rather than calling him an adjutant.

proposals.before: He served as Inspector-and-Protector under Liu Lao's Northern Pacification Army Adjutant.
proposals.after: He served as Inspector-and-Protector under Liu Laozhi, General Who Pacifies the North.
proposals.reason: Same referent and office structure error as in the idiomatic: 牢之 is omitted and 鎮北 is misparsed.

proposals.before: Sima Shufan with Liu Mi, Liu Huaiyu of Pengcheng, and others attacked Zou mountain from Fancheng; when Administrator of Lu Xu Yong lost the city, Zhong led troops to suppress them.
proposals.after: Sima Shufan with Liu Mi and Liu Huaiyu of Pengcheng and others attacked Zou mountain from Fancheng; when Administrator of Lu commandery Xu Yong lost the city, Zhong led troops to suppress them.
proposals.reason: "Administrator of Lu Xu Yong" fuses the commandery name 魯郡 with the person Xu Yong; keep "Administrator of Lu commandery Xu Yong".

proposals.before: When Lu Xun threatened the capital, Xu Chi's army disobeyed orders and was defeated on the south bank.
proposals.after: When Lu Xun threatened the capital, Xu Chijun disobeyed orders and was defeated on the south bank.
proposals.reason: 徐赤軍 is a personal name, not "Xu Chi's army"; 軍 is part of the name.

proposals.before: When Lu Xun pressed the capital, Xu Chi's army disobeyed orders and was defeated on the south bank.
proposals.after: When Lu Xun pressed the capital, Xu Chijun disobeyed orders and was defeated on the south bank.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 徐赤軍 as a person name.

proposals.before: When Lu Xun threatened the capital, Meng Chang, Zhuge Changmin, and others proposed moving the emperor south across the Yangzi. Jin argued before the court that this was unacceptable and openly refuted Chang and his allies; the Founding Emperor was greatly pleased.
proposals.after: When Lu Xun threatened the capital, Meng Chang, Zhuge Changmin, and others proposed moving the emperor south across the Yangzi. Qiujin argued before the court that this was unacceptable and openly refuted Chang and his allies; the Founding Emperor was greatly pleased.
proposals.reason: Silent subject 進 is Yu Qiujin; "Jin" is an unnatural truncation of his name.

proposals.before: More than a thousand men held the old city; Jin advanced, attacked, and captured it.
proposals.after: More than a thousand men held the old city; Qiujin advanced, attacked, and captured it.
proposals.reason: Same truncated short name "Jin" for Yu Qiujin.

proposals.before: Xun then sent Tong Minzhi as Administrator of Poyang to hold the commandery. Jin advanced overland from Yugan toward Poyang; Minzhi fled, and Jin pursued, defeated him, and took several hundred heads.
proposals.after: Xun then sent Tong Minzhi as Administrator of Poyang to hold the commandery. Qiujin advanced overland from Yugan toward Poyang; Minzhi fled, and Qiujin pursued, defeated him, and took several hundred heads.
proposals.reason: Same truncated short name "Jin" for Yu Qiujin.

proposals.before: In the eighth year he was made Protector of the Ningman and Administrator of Xunyang, with civil and military authority. He then followed the campaign against Liu Yi.
proposals.after: In the eighth year he was made Protector of the Ningman and Administrator of Xunyang, holding civil and military authority; two years later he followed the campaign against Liu Yi.
proposals.reason: Chinese 領文武二年從征劉毅 marks a two-year tenure before the Liu Yi campaign; the idiomatic omits 二年.

proposals.before: After the campaign he was appointed Acting Adjutant on the Grand Commandant's staff and soon promoted to General Who Quells Martiality.
proposals.after: After the campaign he was appointed Acting Adjutant on the Grand Commandant's staff and soon promoted to General Who Quells Awe.
proposals.reason: 振威將軍 is not 振武將軍; "Quells Martiality" is the established rendering of 振武, not 振威.

proposals.before: When the affair was settled, he was appointed Acting Adjutant of the Grand Commandant and soon promoted to General Who Quells Martiality.
proposals.after: When the affair was settled, he was appointed Acting Adjutant of the Grand Commandant and soon promoted to General Who Quells Awe.
proposals.reason: Same 振威/振武 confusion in the literal.

decisions.reason: 欽公卒，子彥祖嗣 uses 子, son; the literal's "grandson" invents a generation not in the Chinese, while the idiomatic already has son.
為劉牢之鎮北參軍督護 names Liu Laozhi (牢之) and takes 鎮北 as his title; "Liu Lao" truncates the name and misassigns the adjutant role.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 為劉牢之鎮北參軍督護

decisions.reason: Same structure as the idiomatic: 劉牢之 is Liu Laozhi and 鎮北 is his generalship, not "Liu Lao's Northern Pacification Army Adjutant."
魯郡太守徐邕 is Administrator of Lu commandery Xu Yong; omitting 郡 fuses the commandery into a misleading title string.

decisions.after: When Lu Xun threatened the capital, Xu Chite's army disobeyed orders and was defeated on the south bank.
decisions.reason: "Xu Chi's army" invents the wrong name, but 徐赤軍 is a defective chapter reading; Wikisource and the Zizhi Tongjian parallel have 徐赤特, so the subject is Xu Chite's army, not a person Xu Chijun.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 徐赤特軍違處分，敗于南岸

decisions.after: When Lu Xun pressed the capital, Xu Chite's army disobeyed orders and was defeated on the south bank.
decisions.reason: Same source correction as the idiomatic: restore 徐赤特軍 so 軍 is the army of Xu Chite, not part of a name Xu Chijun.
進廷議不可 is Yu Qiujin speaking; English "Jin" truncates 丘進 into a form that collides with the Jin dynasty name.
In 進攻破之 the subject is again Yu Qiujin (進); "Jin" is the same misleading truncation.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 千餘人守故城，進攻破之

decisions.reason: 進從餘干…追破之 continues Yu Qiujin's actions; both "Jin" tokens should be Qiujin.

decisions.after: In the eighth year he was made Protector of the Ningman and Administrator of Xunyang; leading two thousand civil and military personnel, he followed the campaign against Liu Yi.
decisions.reason: The idiomatic omits material after 領文武, but 二年 is a corruption of 二千: with 八年 above and 九年 below it cannot mean "two years later," as Sun Bin's Songshu kaozheng and Wikisource note.

sourceWitness.citation: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/宋書/卷49 (note 7: 領文武二千從征劉毅)

decisions.after: After the campaign he was appointed Acting Adjutant on the Grand Commandant's staff and soon promoted to General Who Quells Might.
decisions.reason: 振威將軍 is distinct from 振武; Songshu elsewhere renders 振威 as "General Who Quells Might," not "Quells Awe" or "Quells Martiality."

decisions.after: When the affair was settled, he was appointed Acting Adjutant of the Grand Commandant and soon promoted to General Who Quells Might.
decisions.reason: Same 振威 title: use the established Songshu rendering "General Who Quells Might," not the proposed "Quells Awe."

claimRetractions.reason: Accepting r0002 shows English "Liu Lao" was created only by truncating 劉牢之; the correct personal-name Liu Laozhi remains in c0138.
Revising r0005 shows "Xu Chi" was invented by splitting 徐赤軍 into name plus army; the restored reading is Xu Chite's army, not a person Xu Chi.

value.en: Administrator of Lu commandery Xu Yong

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0004 restores 郡 in the English title so it matches 魯郡太守徐邕.
Revised r0005 restores the person as Xu Chite (徐赤特); 軍 belongs to the army phrase, not the given name.
